rgb: The camera wearer stands approximately 3 to 5 m in front of an L-shaped wooden reception counter whose front section spans right-to-left before turning backward along a long hallway extending more than 10 m into the left background, with a white pillar holding fire extinguishers and a wooden lattice screen positioned 0.8 to 1.2 m behind the desk. Arranged from right to left across the counter surface about 3 to 5 m from the camera wearer are a beige-and-brown handbag (out of arm's reach on the right), a small sign, a black monitor facing toward the viewer, a telephone, a receipt printer, a card terminal, a clipboard, and a clear spray bottle. Behind the counter about 3 to 5 m in front of the camera wearer, a woman in a white shirt sits partially occluded from the waist down by the desk and monitor; she leans forward with her hands at the printer in frame 1, sits upright in frames 2 to 4 facing away from the counter while angled and looking slightly toward the left side of the desk, and is mostly cut off by the right frame edge in frame 5. Far to the camera wearer's right (~3 to 5 m away, ~3 to 5 m from the seated woman), a person in a dark purple sleeve has their hands inside the open handbag in frame 1 with their body mostly out of view, disappears past the right border in frames 2 and 5, and has only an arm and the handbag visible at the right edge in frames 3 and 4. At the bottom left edge in frames 2 to 4, an outstretched right hand holding a small card appears about 3 to 5 m away, and in frame 5 the camera turns leftward, shifting the right side of the desk out of view and revealing a person in a red shirt standing 3 to 5 m to the left (~1.5 to 2.0 m from the woman behind the desk), facing away from the counter and looking away from the camera wearer while holding the card over the counter corner out of arm's reach.
depth: The depth map captures the continuous 3D geometry of the reception area, showing a wooden counter in the distant foreground (3 to 5 m away) that recedes alongside a long corridor on the left extending over 5 m into the dark background. Across frames 1 to 4, a person with a handbag stands on the far right at 3 to 5 m (partially cropped out of view in frames 2 to 4) while a receptionist sits behind the counter about 3 to 5 m in front of the camera wearer and roughly 3 to 5 m to the left of the right person, facing away from the counter and camera wearer behind a monitor, telephone, and receipt printer that partially occlude their lower torso. In frames 2 to 4, a hand enters the lower-left foreground at 3 to 5 m, and as the camera wearer turns leftward in frame 5, the receptionist shifts to the far right edge while the person in the red shirt on the left is revealed standing 3 to 5 m away (about 1.5 m from the receptionist), facing and looking away from the camera wearer with their left hand resting on the counter edge. Darker intensities show that the front edge of the counter, the handbag on the right, and the left-hand person's extended hand are out of arm's reach of the camera wearer (3 to 5 m), whereas the monitor, printer, and clipboard sit out of the receptionist's reach. This map makes the smooth distance gradient along the counter surface and corridor wall much clearer than the RGB image alone, though it is unreliable on thin or transparent objects like the spray bottle on the counter (which blurs into the background depth) and flattens fine facial and hand contours into uniform silhouettes.
segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates discrete foreground entities against the unlabelled counter and corridor, localizing the person and handbag on the far right (3 to 5 m away), the seated receptionist in the center-right (3 to 5 m away, facing away from the camera wearer), countertop items in front of the receptionist, and the person on the left (3 to 5 m away, about 1.5 m from the receptionist) who faces and looks away from the camera wearer in frame 5. It shows the receptionist positioned behind and slightly above the counter equipment (labelled as 'laptop') and to the right of the clipboard (labelled as 'book'), with the lower half of the receptionist occluded by the counter and equipment, while the right-hand person is partially out of view at the right frame boundary in frames 1, 3, and 4 and fully out of view in frames 2 and 5. Across the five frames, the masks track the camera wearer's pan to the left, capturing the left-side person initially as just a cropped hand and arm in the lower-left corner of frames 2 and 3 (3 to 5 m away, out of arm's reach of the camera wearer) before revealing their full upper body in frame 5 with a card (labelled as 'remote') out of both their own and the camera wearer's arm's reach. While the masks clearly separate overlapping silhouettes such as the receptionist's torso behind the monitor and the right person's body against the handbag better than raw RGB textures, the map is unreliable in its semantic labels and temporal consistency. Specifically, it misclassifies the desktop monitor and telephone as 'laptop', the clipboard as 'book', the card as 'remote', the handbag in frame 4 as part of a 'person', the wooden lattice screen above the receptionist in frame 4 as a 'tv', and the spray bottle in frame 5 as a 'person' and 'book', while completely missing the receptionist in frame 4.
pose: The body and hand skeleton map tracks sparse 2D joint keypoints and limb orientations in the reception scene, detecting the receptionist's right hand on the counter in frame 1 (about 3 to 5 m away), the receptionist's upper-body skeleton behind the counter in frames 2 and 3 (3 to 5 m away), a distant hand in the lower-left corner of frame 2 (about 3 to 5 m away), and the left-side person's upper body, facial keypoints, and left hand in frame 5 (3 to 5 m away). In frames 2 and 3, the receptionist's shoulder and arm vectors angle forward and downward onto the counter surface out of their arm's reach, with their lower body occluded by the counter and monitor. As the camera wearer turns left by frame 5, the receptionist passes out of the tracked area on the right while the person on the left stands 3 to 5 m in front of the camera wearer (roughly 1.5 m from the receptionist's position), with symmetric shoulder keypoints and centered facial keypoints confirming their torso and head face directly away from the camera wearer while their left arm extends forward and downward to place their magenta-mapped hand on the counter out of arm's reach of both themselves and the camera wearer. The explicit finger and limb segments make exact hand articulation and shoulder orientation easier to read at a glance than in the motion-blurred RGB frames. However, the map is highly unreliable in coverage and stability: it completely misses the person on the far right across all frames, drops the receptionist's skeleton entirely in frames 1, 4, and 5, misses the lower-left hand in frames 3 and 4, and produces distorted, collapsed shoulder-and-head geometry for the receptionist in frames 2 and 3.
